text: Every access decision in Snowflake ultimately traces back to a role. This lesson covers the six roles every account starts with, and how they stack into a hierarchy.
SHOW ROLES lists every role in the account. Pipe the result through RESULT_SCAN on the last query ID and you can filter it like a table — here, down to just the six system-defined roles.

Those six roles each have one job. ORGADMIN manages accounts within an organization. ACCOUNTADMIN is the top-level role — it manages the whole account, so grant it sparingly. SECURITYADMIN manages grants and can manage users and roles. USERADMIN creates and manages users and roles. SYSADMIN creates and owns warehouses, databases, and most objects — it's the role most custom roles should be granted under. And PUBLIC is automatically available to every single user — the implicit base of the hierarchy.

Admin, Users and Roles, Roles tab, Graph view shows this visually. ACCOUNTADMIN sits at the top, connected down to SECURITYADMIN and SYSADMIN, with USERADMIN beneath SYSADMIN. The hierarchy means a role granted to a higher role inherits everything beneath it — ACCOUNTADMIN implicitly has everything SYSADMIN and SECURITYADMIN have.

You can always check which role you're currently using from the Switch Role panel in the user menu — here showing SYSADMIN as the active role. Get in the habit of checking this before you run anything, especially once you start granting privileges in the next lesson.
Next up: RBAC in Snowflake — taking everything you just learned about the system roles and using them to create and grant a custom role of your own.
